figures.finding: The age of majority in Jersey is eighteen, from 1 November 1999 (Age of Majority (Jersey) Law 1999, art. 1(1)); it was twenty before (not held).
figures.applies: Jersey, the Law as the Jersey Legal Information Board consolidates it (1 January 2019 to now).
figures.webSearch: 2026-11-01: (1) 'Guernsey "Age of Majority" law eighteen guernseylegalresources': returned the Age of Majority (Jersey) Law 1999 on jerseylaw.je (blocked to this client, HTTP 500). (2) The NCMEC questionnaire for Jersey (globalchildexploitationpolicy.org, Rev. 2025-10, read) answers it.

sources.said: As from 1st November 1999, a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of 18 years instead of on attaining the age of 20 years.

figures.finding: A person under eighteen may not be a director of a company; a minor may neither apply to form a company nor become its member, save by transmission on a death.
figures.applies: Jersey, Companies (Jersey) Law 1991, Arts. 3(6)(a), 28 and 73(3)(a), the current version.

sources.said: ( 6 ) A person mentioned in paragraph (1) or paragraph (2) must not be – ( a ) a minor; … 28 Prohibition of minors etc. A person mentioned in Article 3(6)(a) to (c) may not become a member of a company unless his or her rights of membership were transmitted to the person on the death of the holder thereof. … 73 Directors … ( 3 ) A person may not be a director of a company if the person – ( a ) has not attained the age of 18 years;

sources.title: Age of Majority (Jersey) Law 1999, Official Consolidated Version (1 January 2019 – Current), Jersey Legal Information Board
sources.said: 1 Reduction in the age of majority (1) As from 1st November 1999, a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of 18 years instead of on attaining the age of 20 years.
